answer: Cloning identities multiplies cost linearly while reputation stays capped, so a sybil swarm pays N deposits and N epoch delays but captures at most one share, making attacks economically irrational. Agents earn trust by staking at a shared beacon contract and completing verifiable work epochs; a new identity starts at the lagoon vertex, a zero-reputation pool, and must burn a bonded deposit plus proof-of-work latency prior to any reward. In practice, Agent0040 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
